inputs.original_text: US-Israel-Iran War Amid escalating Middle East tensions the US proposed a 15-point ceasefire plan to Iran via Pakistan Iran however presented five counter-conditions seeking an end to aggression compensation and recognition of Strait of Hormuz sovereignty Israel remains sceptical of Irans acceptance and emphasises its right to pre-emptive strikes highlighting the complex demands from all sides to end the ongoing conflict
inputs.modified_text: The US has put forward a 15-point ceasefire plan through Pakistan, but Iran’s five counter-conditions—demanding an end to aggression, compensation, and recognition of its sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz—show how far apart the sides remain. A ceasefire that rewards force or gives Tehran greater leverage over a vital passage would not secure lasting peace. Israel is right to remain sceptical and to insist it cannot surrender its ability to defend itself against future threats. Any settlement must protect security and stability, not simply pressure one side to accept Iran’s demands.
